title: Shipping Time Calculator: Transit Estimates
description: Estimate a shipment's transit time from route distance and vessel or vehicle speed with the Shipping Time Calculator — honestly framed. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 5,800-nautical-mile sea leg at 16 knots is about 15.1 days of sailing — before the port days at both ends that real shipping adds.
quick_answer: The Shipping Time Calculator estimates a shipment's time in transit from the route distance and the carrier's speed, in the units freight uses. Enter the distance and the speed and read the transit time — the moving part of a delivery estimate, separated honestly from the handling days around it.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
Transit time: route distance ÷ speed, in hours and days — the moving leg of a shipment's journey.
Is it free to use?
Yes, for estimates and quote-checking alike.
How accurate is the result?
Exact for the distance and speed entered — and explicitly incomplete as a delivery date: handling, customs, port time and last-mile are separate additions.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Congestion at sea is weather and ports; on road, hours-of-service. Neither lives inside a distance ÷ speed estimate, and this page does not pretend otherwise.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Freight travels networks, not geometry. Enter the route distance the shipment will actually move.
Why is my carrier's quote longer?
Because it includes everything this estimate excludes — consolidation, handling, customs, schedules that sail twice a week. The gap is explainable, and now measurable.
Air freight?
The division works with air distances and speeds too, though air schedules are built from flight blocks and cut-off times — treat the result as the flying floor of the estimate.
Why do quotes say 'transit time' so precisely?
Because it is the part carriers control. The vaguer words around it (handling, customs) are where the honesty of a quote is tested.
Incoterms and responsibility?
Who bears the transit risk is a contract matter above this calculator's pay grade — it computes time, not liability.
Can it compare air versus sea?
Run both legs' figures: the division gives each mode's motion time, and the comparison is usually measured in weeks versus days.
